card: This PR adds [[nodiscard]] attributes to legacy getter functions that return a boolean success code alongside mutable out-parameters, preventing callers from accidentally ignoring retrieval failures. It also fixes call sites where return values were previously ignored, including adding an assertion in witness sigop counting and checking cache retrieval results in descriptor evaluation. Reviewers will need to verify whether the assertion in script interpretation is guaranteed safe under all valid and invalid inputs.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the complete diff, confirming specific call-site fixes in `interpreter.cpp`, `descriptor.cpp`, and `transaction_tests.cpp` alongside header annotations across 22 files.
evidence: Compiler warnings highlighted previously unchecked calls that now require inspection: `ignoring return value of function declared with 'nodiscard' attribute [-Wunused-result]` (commit messages b7cde58e16 and 6ae45f7795)
PR description: 'To ensure that the "imaginary optional" is not unwrapped when the getter returns false, add a C++17 [[nodiscard]] attribute to all those legacy functions.'
problem: Legacy getters using the `bool Get...(..., mut& out)` pattern allow callers to silently discard return values and inspect uninitialized or invalid out-parameters when retrieval fails.

risk.why: Adding an `Assert` in consensus-critical script interpretation (`CountWitnessSigOps`) could crash the node during block validation if the premise that `GetOp` never returns false after `IsPushOnly` fails.

scope_notes: Touches headers across multiple subsystems (wallet, script, net processing, interfaces) mechanically, but includes behavioral changes at call sites: adding an `Assert(...)` in `CountWitnessSigOps` in `interpreter.cpp` and checking the return value in descriptor caching logic.
summary: Annotate legacy getter functions that return a boolean success flag alongside mutable out-parameters with the C++17 `[[nodiscard]]` attribute across the codebase. Update or assert callers that previously ignored the return value in descriptor cache lookups, unit tests, and witness sigop counting.
